chapter: Armstrong, Parker and life inside the Basie band
title: Practicing then and now
summary: Tate says he practised all day when young, less with Basie, and now nearly as much as ever.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I did then. Yeah, I used to, all day.
At what point did you stop or do you still practice?

Well, not as much as I used to. I -- well, actually, well, I would say, after I joined in Basie -- you know, we played every night. So I didn't have a chance, you know. But I practice more now than I did when I was with Basie's band, because I have days off and I have time in my home and I have all the chances now, you know, because I can practice as long as I would like and it doesn't bother anybody, like an apartment. Sometime people get kind of drug with you, you know.

But now, I practice more now, I think, just about almost as much as I did when I was really trying to, you know, play, when I was really trying to get with it, you know. But it's very important. I don't care how much you know, it's very important, because everytime you pick up your horn, you learn something. I guess that's the fascinating part about it, because it's really interesting, you know, because everytime
you pick it up, it's something you can, you know, you can learn.
